chapter_title: Concerning the Sect of the Basket
chapter_note: Chapter has a clear two-part structure: (1) paragraphs 1-4 are a narrative encounter with a presbyter from a non-Manichaean sect, entirely institutional/editorial/exhortatory material including polemic and a beatitude identification of 'basket' with 'holy church'; (2) paragraphs 5-6 contain heavily fragmentary but recognizable cosmological teaching — cosmic architecture (pillars, disk, sea), cosmic beings (Mind, Youth, Porter, five sons of the Man, Adamant of Light), and cosmic enumerations (thirty-six, twenty-two, twelve, seven, four). The substrate is NOT dominant — it survives only in the latter, very damaged portion. Teaching purity is low (0.254). The editorial fatigue pattern is inverted here — substrate increases in the second half (+5.39), suggesting the cosmological teaching was appended or preserved at the end while the first half was fully replaced by narrative polemic. Gardner's uncertainty about the chapter's coherence is justified — the connection between the sect discussion and the cosmological catalogue is unclear.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure narrative frame formula: 'Once again, on one of the occasions, as our enlightener is sitting' followed by narrative setting in Babylon. High dialogue_frame (15.52) and institutional (17.24) scores confirm. 'A presbyter belonging to the [sect] of the basket' and 'worshipper of idols' are narrative identifications, not cosmological teaching.

Heavily lacunose discussion of the sect's name and practices — fruit hanging from trees, grapes, vine, apples, basket. All register scores at zero. This describes a specific sect's identity and practices (possibly fruitarian, per Gardner). No cosmological mapping; the fruit/tree language here is about literal agricultural practice, not cosmic correspondence.

Opens with dialogue frame attribution ('The apostle speaks to the presbyter of the sect of the basket:'). The content is a rhetorical argument using simile (universe 'like a tree', person 'like fruit') addressed to 'you' (the presbyter). This is polemic directed at a specific sect — one side of the mapping reaches into the presbyter's contemporary situation ('how then do you call yourself the son of the basket'). Not systematic cosmological mapping but rhetorical use of analogy for institutional polemic. The concept of being 'entangled in the universe' is cosmological vocabulary repurposed for argument.

Beatitude formula ('B[less]ed [...] the children of the basket') is the structural marker of the exhortation layer. Wraps strongly institutional content: alms-giving, renunciation of possessions ('from the houses, from the gold and silver'), and the climactic institutional identification 'which is the holy church!' Functions as devotional closure to the polemic section (¶2-3). 'He raised his hand to his disciples' is a narrative gesture transitioning from addressing the presbyter to addressing the community.

paragraphs.core_text: The [...] and the great [...] and the great Mind that is [...] this Youth that is with the [...] thirty-six angels [...] twenty-two angels [...] but [...] of the twenty-two [...] ⟨p.290⟩ the seven pillars that stan[d ...] the sea that surrounds the universe [...] four angels that are distributed to the [...] universe, supporting the mightiness [...] below, which is the earth of all the heavens [...] these other five gods, the sons of the Man, they that [...] the universe is stood firm [...] the summons and the obedience [...] the splendour of the [...] the Adamant of Light [...] they are become enemies [...] they guide it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Then he says to him [...]' (dialogue frame attribution). Removed 'holy church and' from 'the splendour of the [...] holy church and the Adamant of Light' — institutional insertion into a cosmological list, likely editorial addition linking the cosmic catalogue to the Manichaean institution. The Adamant of Light is a cosmic entity; 'holy church' was inserted alongside it by the compiler.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Dense cosmological catalogue despite heavy lacunae. Identifiable substrate entities: the great Mind (Nous), the Youth (Third Messenger figure), thirty-six and twenty-two angels (cosmic enumerations), seven pillars (cosmic architecture), the sea surrounding the universe (cosmic geography), four supporting angels, the earth of all the heavens, five gods/sons of the Man (five sons of Primal Man), the summons and the obedience (the Call and Answer pair), the Adamant of Light. Substrate score 10.83 confirms. 'Holy church' disrupts an otherwise cosmic list — classic editorial seam inserting institutional identity into substrate enumeration.

paragraphs.core_text: The third also, [...] below, there are twelve powers standing firm there. However, the number of the twelve images [...] the three great pillars of mightiness that [...] pillars supporting the disk [...] the other three [...] they are the garments that the Living Spirit [...] he put them at that time [...] that threw them, together with [...] which is displayed therein [...] this [...] perfect before [...] great Porter [...] in his power [...] these are the three great [...] against [...] are in the midst of people [...] knows [...] entrusts his soul to them [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the cosmic architecture catalogue. 'The third also' is an enumeration marker continuing from ¶5's teaching sequence. Substrate entities: twelve powers, twelve images (cosmic correspondences), three great pillars of mightiness (cosmic architecture), pillars supporting the disk (the cosmic disk/earth-plate), the Living Spirit (Mihryazd — major cosmic emanation), the great Porter (Atlas-figure supporting the worlds). Low substrate score (2.02) likely reflects vocabulary pipeline limitations with heavily lacunose text. The ending 'are in the midst of people [...] knows [...] entrusts his soul to them' is ambiguous — could be editorial bridge reaching into the human world, but too fragmentary to determine. Preserved with uncertainty noted.
